summary: Discovery call focused on model selection trade-offs for a hybrid deployment. Cobalt needs multilingual support, long-context sessions for documents (32k+ preference), tool-calling/function support, and clarity around hosted vs dedicated vs private (security, latency, cost). AE + SE covered performance profiles, quantization options, and next steps to run benchmarks.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-16 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Eli Chen (CTO, Cobalt Ventures), Rina Kapoor (ML Lead), Samir Patel (Infra)

Summary (auto): model selection, context length, multilingual, tool-calling, hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. We've got Diego, our solutions engineer, on for the deep dive. Quick intros?
[00:08] Eli: Eli here, CTO. Rina is ML lead, Samir on infra. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for a new document assistant product.
[00:15] Maya: Great, high level can you share primary success criteria and any blockers?
[00:22] Rina: Main things — multilingual support (EN/ES/DE/JA), large documents up to ~200k tokens ideally over multiple passes but first pass needs 32k context. Also tool-calling — we need function calls to kick off SQL lookups and internal search. Cost matters but latency SLO around 200-400ms for short queries.
[00:36] Diego: ok, so two classes: short interactive queries and long-document syntheses. Are you expecting streaming for the short queries?
[00:43] Rina: yes, streaming is preferred for UX.
[00:46] Samir: security — SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS for key management, VPC peering or private link. Data residency EU for some customers.
[00:56] Maya: Understood. For model selection, we typically consider open model variants with different context lengths and token efficiency — e.g., 8k/32k/100k context families. We can map workloads to hosted, dedicated or private. Quick question: are you okay using a quantized model for production? We can do int8 or int4 to reduce cost but impacts quality slightly.
[01:16] Rina: We're open to quantization if quality remains acceptable on our eval prompts. We'll share prompts.
[01:22] Eli: Also want to avoid vendor lock in — prefer open or widely supported model formats.
[01:27] Diego: Good. On Redwood hosted we run curated open models with verified perf profiles — low friction but data flows through our infra with optional retention controls. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity on similar hardware (A100/H100) with predictable throughput. Private is customer-controlled with our private control plane, suitable for strict residency and KMS/HSM integration.
[01:46] Samir: What about latency? If we go dedicated or private do we get lower tail latency?
[01:52] Diego: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor effects and you can size for throughput; private can be even closer to your network if colocated, but depends on your infra. We typically see 10-20% lower p95 on dedicated vs shared hosted for similar instance types.
[02:05] Rina: For model families — can you compare tradeoffs between Mistral-like models, Llama variants, and the newer long context open models?
[02:13] Diego: Sure — quick high level: Mistral models tend to be cost-efficient with strong single-turn quality; Llama-like (meta) families have broader toolchain support and many community quantization recipes; long-context families (100k) trade compute for memory and require different kernel scheduling. For your long-document workflow we might recommend a 32k family for interactive sessions and a 100k family for full doc ingestion.
[02:38] Eli: Any specifics about function/tool calling support? We need deterministic function calls that map to our internal APIs.
[02:45] Diego: Most open families support function calling when wrapped in our runtime; we provide structured tool-calling with schema enforcement and can log the call payloads to your audit logs. Note: sometimes tokenization around function names and args can vary across models, we sometimes see subtle differences that affect extraction — we do a small compatibility pass during pilot.
[03:04] Rina: Good, we'll need that compatibility pass. Also multilingual — do you recommend different models per language or a single multilingual model?
[03:11] Diego: If you need top-tier quality for each language, specialized models can help, but modern multilingual families are pretty solid. For EU residency it might be better to pin a vetted multilingual model on dedicated/private to avoid cross-region variance.
[03:25] Eli: On cost, can you ballpark hosted pricing vs dedicated commit for an expected 10M tokens/month?
[03:32] Maya: We’ll send a detailed pricing matrix — rough thumb rule: hosted per-token tends to be a bit higher but no infra overhead; dedicated with reserved capacity lowers per-token compute cost but has monthly commit. We'll include sample numbers in the matrix.
[03:46] Samir: Networking: will private deployment require our infra team to open ports? We also use Okta SAML for SSO.
[03:53] Diego: Private deploys usually involve VPC peering or PrivateLink, direct peering for low-latency. SSO via SAML/Okta supported; KMS integrations (AWS KMS / Azure KeyVault / on-prem HSM) are supported in private and dedicated with different guarantees.
[04:07] Rina: We also want to run model comparisons on our prompts — quality metrics + latency + cost. Can Redwood run benchmarks or do we run locally?
[04:15] Diego: We can run an initial benchmark on our hosted infra with your prompts (sanitized) and also provide the test harness so you can run locally in a private pilot. For pilot we typically do 1) perf on hosted, 2) perf on dedicated instance type, 3) private smoke test.
[04:30] Eli: About context — you mentioned 100k models require different kernel scheduling. Does Redwood support chunked prefix caching or persistent KV cache across sessions?
[04:40] Diego: Yes — runtime supports KV cache management and prefix caching; for multi-pass doc processing we recommend hybrid approach: chunk + retrieval + KV prefix for hot segments. Also we have automatic batching controls to keep latency SLOs while improving throughput.
[04:58] Rina: Is there a recommended model for few-shot synthesis in Japanese? We've seen tokenization artifacts with some open models.
[05:05] Diego: We can test a couple; often the tokenizers vary — we do tokenizer normalization steps and can provide guidance. We'll add specific models to the matrix.
[05:13] Maya: I'm going to share a model selection sheet after this call. It will show latency, cost, tokenization quirks, multilingual bench results, and recommended deployment mode.
[05:21] Eli: For tool-calling reliability — how do you surface failed calls? We need end-to-end tracing into our monitoring stack.
[05:29] Diego: We capture tool-call logs, response status, and can forward traces via open telemetry / datadog. On private deployments we can ship logs to your S3 or SIEM.
[05:38] Samir: Any regulatory issues with using hosted for EU customers? Data residency is the big one.
[05:43] Maya: Hosted can be used if you engage regional controls and retention options; for strict residency and KMS control, private is the safest. We also have enterprise contracts to define data handling.
[05:52] Rina: Timeline — we hope to get a pilot running in the next 4 weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:57] Diego: Yes, if we get your prompt set and infra constraints this week we can provision a pilot — hosted is fastest (days), dedicated takes a little longer (capacity sizing), private depends on your infra team but typically 2-4 weeks.
[06:10] Eli: Ok, let's talk about some technical details — Samir, any network constraints?
[06:13] Samir: Our infra team restricts outbound only via proxy and we use peered AWS accounts in eu-west-1. We'll need a design that works with VPC peering.
[06:20] Diego: We can do VPC peering or PrivateLink; we'll share a diagram.
[06:24] Rina: On evaluations, we'll measure ROUGE/BLEU where applicable, also embedding cosine sim for search quality. Do you have metric recipes?
[06:32] Maya: Yes, we'll include our eval recipes and a recommended set of thresholds.
[06:36] [crosstalk] Eli: — and if we need model updates mid-pilot what's the process?
[06:39] Diego: We support pinned versions and rollouts; can do canary vs full rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if regressions occur.
[06:48] Rina: Any limits on streaming tokens for long contexts?
[06:52] Diego: Streaming for very long contexts becomes tricky — we stream incremental completions and can stream partial tokens; for 100k ingest/analysis workflows we usually chunk and stream summaries.
[07:02] Maya: ok let's go through a quick recency check — key blockers are: security/KMS, private networking, multilingual tokenizer edge cases, and cost/latency tradeoffs. Anything to add?
[07:14] Eli: Need to confirm EU data residency and pilot timeline.
[07:19] Samir: Confirm SSO (Okta) and proxy requirements.
[07:22] Rina: We'll share prompt sets and evaluation criteria.
[07:25] Maya: Great — next steps are in the action items. Diego will run an initial hosted bench with your prompts, and we'll share matrix + pricing.
[07:34] Diego: One note — regarding quantization: int8 usually safe, int4 can be aggressive and sometimes hurts multilingual nuance; we'll include both in the bench.
[07:46] Rina: Good to know.
[07:48] Eli: Any competitors we should be worried about? We've seen demos from Anthropic and some custom self-hosted setups.
[07:54] Maya: We see Anthropic and OpenAI in demo flows, Mistral in open model space; our differentiator is unified runtime + deployment flexibility + observability.
[08:03] Samir: For the pilot, what telemetry do you need from our side?
[08:07] Diego: We'll need sample traffic shape, prompt set, and target latency/cost numbers. Also API keys or peering details if private.
[08:15] Rina: We'll send prompts by EOD Thursday.
[08:18] Maya: Perfect. Anything else before we wrap?
[08:22] Eli: No, that's it. Thanks all.
[08:25] Maya: Thanks everyone — recap in the email with links to the matrix, security docs, and proposed pilot schedule.
[08:30] Diego: I'll attach the private deployment checklist and KMS integration notes.
[08:33] Maya: End call.

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hearings around "KV cache" (appears as "kay vee cache" in raw), occasional dropped punctuation. References: model selection spreadsheet (link), private deployment checklist (link), benchmark harness (link).
